study.title: Acupuncture Alters Brain's Dynamic Functional Network Connectivity in Stroke Patients with Motor Dysfunction: A Randomised Controlled Neuroimaging Trial
study.randomization: randomly divided into the true acupoint treatment group (TATG) and the sham acupoint treatment group (SATG) at a ratio of 2:1 using a random number table
study.blinding: patients and assessors blinded for group allocation
study.population: ischemic stroke patients with motor dysfunction
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) patients with ischemic stroke; (2) within 6 weeks from onset; (3) single lesion of ischemic infarct restricted to the unilateral hemisphere involving the internal capsule, basal ganglia, corona radiata, and its neighboring regions; (4) right-handed before stroke; (5) 35-80 years of age; (6) consciousness and stable condition; (7) not taken any psychiatric medications in 1 month
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) severe primary diseases of heart, liver, kidneys, hematologic system, immune system disease, tumors, and psychiatric disorders; (2) pregnant or lactating women; (3) any MRI contraindications; (4) any brain abnormalities except infarction identified by MRI

arms.dropouts: 10 excluded: 5 did not complete second MRI scan for personal reasons, 5 excluded due to severe head motion during scanning
3 excluded: 1 did not complete second MRI scan for personal reasons, 2 excluded due to severe head motion during scanning

conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: The sham condition uses real acupuncture needles (Ande brand disposable) at non-acupoint locations 20mm beside true acupoints, with De qi sensations explicitly avoided. However, neither insertion depth nor penetration status is reported. While real needles suggest likely penetration, the avoidance of De qi could imply very superficial insertion or no insertion at all. Without depth information, tissue level cannot be determined. | RESOLVED: needling at non-acupoints with depth not stated → assumed Level 1 (standard clinical depth)

Same sham protocol as SATG_pre: real acupuncture needles at non-acupoint locations 20mm beside true acupoints, De qi avoided, but depth and penetration not reported. Identical reasoning applies — tissue level cannot be classified without explicit depth information. | RESOLVED: needling at non-acupoints with depth not stated → assumed Level 1 (standard clinical depth)

extraction_notes.note: No quantitative measurement of deqi/sensory responses was reported for either group. The paper only describes De qi qualitatively ('soreness, dullness, numbness, heaviness') for TATG and states it was avoided in SATG. No MASS or VAS scores for sensations were reported.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success were not assessed or reported. The paper does not mention any instrument for assessing patient expectancy or credibility of intervention.
Adverse events were not reported. The paper does not mention any adverse event monitoring or occurrence.

Specific IC pairs showing significant connectivity changes within TATG state 3 (FPN-SMN) and state 2 (RFPN-SMN) are visible in Figure 5 but the exact IC numbers (e.g., IC 41, 48, 1, 12, 45, 50) involved in each significant pair are only discernible from the figure matrices. Exact asterisk positions in figure are readable from description but specific node-pair t/p statistics are not tabulated.
The probability map and detailed information of the lesion location in each patient, and the location of all acupoints are shown in Supplementary Material 1, which was not provided.
Validation analysis results (different window lengths and cluster numbers) are shown in Supplementary Material 2, which was not provided.

The paper reports 'reduced FC between FPN and SMN in state 3' in TATG after treatment, but the specific sub-networks (LFPN vs RFPN) involved in this contrast in state 3 are partially described (RFPN-SMN in state 2 noted separately) and the complete set of significant IC pairs in state 3 for TATG is only available in Figure 5c, which shows multiple asterisks.

For the between-group ANCOVA comparison of connectivity strength, the paper only reports significance for DAN-RFPN in state 1 (positive effect). It is unclear whether other connectivity pairs were tested but not significant, or were not compared.
The paper states that sham acupoints were 20mm beside the true acupoints but does not provide explicit details on needle insertion depth or whether needles penetrated the skin in the sham condition.

The validation analysis mentions that number of transitions significantly increased after treatment in the TATG group when k=3 clusters and W=22TRs sliding window, but this was not among the primary results and statistical values are not provided in the main text.
No PMID was found in the paper. DOI is 10.1155/2023/8510213 as stated in the article header.

In the TATG group, Table 4 shows all temporal parameters with pre/post values and t/p statistics; however fraction time state 2 and mean dwell time state 1 and state 2 and number of transitions are all non-significant (P > 0.05). Only mean dwell time state 3 (p=0.046) is significant after FDR correction for TATG. For SATG only mean dwell time state 2 (p=0.038) is significant after FDR correction.
